description: We are a passionate, multidisciplinary team of problem-solvers, creators, and space enthusiasts united by a common mission: to tackle real-world challenges using Earth and space data. By combining our diverse skills in technology, science, and design, we aim to build innovative, practical solutions that make a positive impact both on Earth and beyond.
summary:
LUNAWINDOW is an interactive lunar exploration browser designed to help users examine and compare potential Moon exploration locations through key geometric factors: sunlight conditions and visibility of Earth. The project provides a visual interface for managing candidate locations, viewing simplified solar and Earth elevation indicators, comparing sites, and exporting candidate data.

By bringing these factors together in one accessible browser-based tool, LUNAWINDOW helps make lunar site exploration concepts easier to understand and investigate. It is designed as an educational and early-stage exploration aid, not as a certified landing-site selection or mission-safety system. Its current calculations use idealized lunar geometry, with terrain effects and full mission-grade ephemeris integration identified as future improvements.
details:
LUNAWINDOW is a browser-based lunar exploration workspace built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It allows users to create lunar candidate locations by entering latitude and longitude or selecting points on a schematic lunar globe. Each candidate can be inspected, renamed, deleted, compared with other candidates, and exported.

The application calculates first-order solar elevation, solar incidence angle, and Earth elevation using vector geometry on an idealized spherical Moon. It uses the dot product between a candidate's surface-normal vector and an assumed direction vector to estimate elevation. It also provides a NASA/JPL Horizons reference-data workflow: users can retrieve Moon-centered Sun and Earth vectors from the official Horizons service and import the returned JSON for inspection.

The project focuses on making important geometric considerations in lunar exploration understandable and accessible. It includes candidate comparison, CSV/report export, browser-based local storage, and a scientific methods and limitations section.

The current version is an exploratory prototype, not a validated landing-site selection system. It does not yet transform inertial vectors into a lunar body-fixed coordinate frame, model detailed terrain or local shadows, or calculate communications, thermal, power, or landing hazards.

Development involved HTML, CSS, JavaScript, browser local storage, Netlify hosting, and AI-assisted coding and writing. The project was designed and assembled as an original participant project, with AI assistance acknowledged in the submission.
